externalReview.visualInspection: One-page official curriculum diagram inspected; each component and credit value reconciled with canonical list. Repeated 7-EC project in two blocks counted once.

routeRule.basis: The generic Bedrijfskunde programme has three formal third-year tracks. Entrepreneurship is explicitly central across the first two years, including venture creation, innovation and growth, so Entrepreneurship for Growth most directly continues the programme-wide academic identity. The choice is independent of UCR fit.

conditions: Complete B1 60 EC before third-year choice-space/track registration.
One complete track; no mixing modules; allocation capacity-limited.
30 EC choice plus 3 EC Advanced Research Skills in blocks 3.1–3.3; remaining core/track 27 EC.
Selected minor/electives route has no compulsory internship.
externalReview.marketingInconsistencies: The overview includes inconsistent four/five-block and five/three-track wording. Use the July-2026 curriculum and September-2026 B3 pages: three current tracks; do not import obsolete overview counts.

academicReview.strongestChallenge: A generic coherent LAS curriculum would not be sufficient. These programmes retain substantive entrepreneurship, strategy, accounting, economics and management/research content. Sustainability applications and computational planning are complements with stated scope, not proxies for the full RSM business-functions sequence.

programmes.concept: Business foundations, strategy and marketing connect with leadership, organisational psychology and international business. Accounting, economics, research methods and data analysis support the study of firms and management decisions.
programmes.assessment: Broad business foundations and management are substantial; preserve all 24 course choices.

programmes.concept: Business strategy, marketing, organisational behaviour and ethical leadership connect with climate, life-cycle assessment and circular resource use. Technical study of materials, farming and renewable energy supplies specific applications for evaluating sustainable business decisions.
programmes.assessment: The independently evidenced sustainable-business direction integrates business strategy, marketing, organisational psychology, law and ethics with LCA, circular materials and applied energy/food-system evidence; preserve its technical studies with bounded roles.

programmes.concept: Accounting, financial decisions and economics connect with econometrics, probability, data science and machine learning. Programming, databases and AI planning provide computational tools, while strategy, negotiation and international business supply managerial context.
programmes.assessment: The independently evidenced finance direction integrates financial decisions, accounting, economics and quantitative inquiry. AI planning is a method complement, not a replacement business discipline; preserve all choices with better statistical progression.

stopping.assessment: Two additional generator-backed directions are coherent and feasible after the closest match: Sustainable Business Strategies and Financial Analysis & Investment. Both produce curricula that are substantively distinct and exceed the 30-EC pairwise floor, so the maximum of three UCR alternatives is reached.

changedPartialCorrespondences.b2-innovation: Product design develops innovation through customer needs, prototyping, costing and environmental assessment; it is narrower than a general Innovation Management course.
changedPartialCorrespondences.b2-resplead: The UCR course focuses on inclusive leadership and diversity. It contributes to responsible leadership without covering the full RSM organisational-responsibility course.
changedPartialCorrespondences.b3-research: Market Research provides applied research design, data collection and analysis in a marketing setting; it does not reproduce the whole general management-research and literature-review course.
changedPartialCorrespondences.b3-methods: Econometrics provides causal/predictive regression and inference, using Stata. The RSM course also includes R, panel/time-series methods, introductory machine learning and optimisation; the courses are partial counterparts.
changedPartialCorrespondences.b1-math: Mathematical Methods provides calculus and differential-equation techniques, including economic applications; the exact business-mathematics syllabus is not claimed to be identical.
changedPartialCorrespondences.b2-techmgmt: The UCR course examines the business and governance implications of AI; it covers a particular technological domain rather than all of technology management.
changedPartialCorrespondences.b1-infomgmt: Database Management Systems provides relational data structures and SQL; its technical scope is narrower than general business information management.
changedPartialCorrespondences.b3-cross: International Business & Governance includes cultural and institutional forces shaping firms; it is broader in governance and does not reproduce dedicated cross-cultural management training.
changedPartialCorrespondences.b1-profdev: PPD provides first-year personal, collaborative and academic formation; its LAS setting differs from RSM business mentoring.
